prior: W-R65 independently classified MIXED_OR_NONREPLICATION; shifting or reversing channel0 and channel1 separately both hurt accuracy, so source0-exclusive temporal causality unsupported.
hypothesis: Does shifting all 4 channels together recover accuracy relative to breaking individual channel timing (cross-channel alignment), or is the fixed readout intrinsically sensitive to absolute within-channel temporal ordering?
freeze: Use W-R65/W-R61 frozen three ridge fits, feature width 16, withheld xorshift source/entities9..17, amplitudes 1/2/3, four acquisition permutations, and fixed development blocks. Change only input timing interventions, no model training. Apply transformations identically to baseline, positive and negative exemplars; zero time-index wrap; preserve each channel's values.
primary: 288 intervention cells = three fixed models x three amplitudes x four permutations x eight conditions, each across 24 fresh sealed seeds. Compare 36 paired mean changes against intact. SYNCHRONOUS_ALIGNMENT_RESCUE iff source0 and source1 individual shifts each <= -0.06, shift_all >= -0.04, and shift_all at least 0.04 less adverse than either individual shift. NO_GLOBAL_ALIGNMENT_RESCUE iff both individual shifts <= -0.06 and shift_all <= -0.06. Else MIXED_OR_INCONCLUSIVE.
controls: Circular shifts and reversals preserve marginal channel value multisets
All-channel and paired-channel perturbations plus original source0 reversal
W65 identical acquisition permutations and source-withheld models
One original first use and full regression; independent archive-only readback
claim_limit: Frozen synthetic channel order/alignment distinction; not demonstrated cognition, general transfer, or RSI.
